title: ABO Blood Group System: Basics and Forward/Reverse Typing
summary: ABO antigens and antibodies, forward and reverse grouping, and how to resolve discrepancies before issuing blood.
objectives: Explain the biochemical basis of A and B antigens on red cells.
Perform and interpret forward and reverse ABO typing.
Recognize and start resolving ABO discrepancies.

highYield: Group A red cells carry A antigen; plasma contains anti-B.
Group O red cells carry neither A nor B antigen; plasma contains anti-A and anti-B.
A discrepancy between forward and reverse typing must be resolved before issuing blood.
quickReview.mnemonic: O has nO antigens and bOth antibodies.

deepStudy.introduction: The ABO system is the most important blood group system in transfusion medicine because naturally occurring IgM antibodies against absent A/B antigens cause rapid complement-mediated intravascular hemolysis.

sections.heading: Molecular basis
sections.body: A and B antigens are produced by glycosyltransferases encoded by the ABO gene on chromosome 9. The A transferase adds N-acetylgalactosamine; the B transferase adds D-galactose to the H substance. Group O individuals have a nonfunctional enzyme and leave the H substance unmodified.

sections.heading: Forward and reverse typing
sections.body: Forward typing tests patient red cells with known anti-A and anti-B reagents. Reverse typing tests patient serum/plasma with known A1 and B reagent red cells. Both must agree before a blood type is reported. Newborns have weak reverse typing because antibodies are of maternal origin or not yet produced.

sections.heading: Subgroups and secretors
sections.body: A subgroups (A1, A2) differ in the amount of A antigen. Anti-A1 lectin (Dolichos biflorus) identifies A1 cells. Secretors (FUT2 gene) secrete soluble ABH substances in body fluids.

deepStudy.clinicalSignificance: ABO-incompatible transfusion causes acute hemolytic transfusion reaction — a leading cause of transfusion fatalities. ABO-identical plasma is required because plasma contains isohemagglutinins.
deepStudy.labInterpretation: Always confirm the ABO group on two samples for pretransfusion testing when policy requires; investigate every forward/reverse discrepancy before component release.
examTraps: Reverse typing in newborns is weak/absent because antibodies are maternal IgG or not yet produced — do not expect concordance in infants under 4 months.
Acquired B (e.g., in bowel obstruction) can make group A cells type as AB — look at the patient's history and plasma reactions.

memoryHooks.funny: Meow: 'nO antigens, bOth antibodies — like a cat with no manners and all the opinions.'

memoryHooks.text: Forward types the cells; reverse types the serum.
memoryHooks.funny: Forward = cells first. Parang pag-crush: kilalanin mo muna ang tao (cells), tapos ang feelings (serum).
